sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite Model Card (September 26, 2025)
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and inspected the complete nine-page September 26, 2025 card. Its architecture section identifies sparse MoE routing that activates a subset of experts per token, without a numerical total or active size. The evaluation and safety tables distinguish June 17 Flash-Lite from the September preview and disclose no parameter counts.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Exact stable ID gemini-2.5-flash-lite: 1,048,576 input tokens; text, image, video, audio and PDF inputs; text output; thinking and function calling supported. Page updated September 22, 2026 describes access limited to previous users; this is documentation, not an endpoint test. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit; the exact stable-model specification table contains no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: We’re expanding our Gemini 2.5 family of models
sources.evidence: June 17, 2025 announcement makes the Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite public preview available through AI Studio and Vertex AI, establishing the earliest public release.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite is now stable and generally available
sources.evidence: July 22, 2025 announcement introduces stable gemini-2.5-flash-lite and explicitly says it is the same underlying model as the prior preview. It documents optional reasoning, million-token context and use through AI Studio and Vertex AI. Reopened October 27: the June-preview-to-stable identity is explicit, but neither version is assigned a numerical size; no named base with a disclosed count is identified.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Google’s proprietary API terms govern model access and prohibit extracting model components, including parameter weights. No open-weight license is offered by these service terms.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
sources.evidence: Fresh full PDF retrieved October 27, 2026. Section 2.1 describes sparse MoE routing without numerical total, expert, or active counts. The same section describes teacher-output distillation for Flash-sized and smaller models, which is a training relationship rather than a claim that the student shares a teacher parameter count. The report explicitly discusses gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-06-17 on pages 10–11; Table 1 covers 2.5 Pro/Flash and 2.0 Flash-Lite. Neither that exact-model passage nor the remaining tables supplies a Flash-Lite size. The 22B vision-transformer and trillion-parameter Switch references are other research, not specifications for this model.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Model Card (March 2026)
sources.evidence: Fresh full card retrieved October 27, 2026. Its March 2026 comparison explicitly includes Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite Dynamic and reports pricing, output speed, benchmark scores, and context performance; there is no total-parameter or activated-parameter row/column. The separate statement that Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is based on Gemini 3 Pro does not identify a base for Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite Model Card (July 2026)
sources.evidence: Fresh full card retrieved October 27, 2026. The July 2026 comparison covers Gemini 3.5/3.1 Flash-Lite and other providers; it supplies no retrospective 2.5 Flash-Lite parameter specification. Its explicit 3.5-to-3.1 model dependency does not establish the size or lineage of this older 2.5 model.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card (October 2026)
sources.evidence: Fresh complete October 2026 card retrieved October 27 and inspected after gzip decoding. Architecture and evaluation sections contain no numerical parameter specification or retrospective disclosure for Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite; Argon is explicitly a new model, not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model.

sources.title: Model versions and lifecycle — Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
sources.evidence: Lists gemini-2.5-flash-lite stable release on July 22, 2025 and Agent Platform retirement on October 20, 2026. Stable ID release is distinguished from the earlier preview of the same model.

sources.title: Learn about supported models — Firebase AI Logic
sources.evidence: Lists July 22, 2025 as the stable ID release and shutdown warnings for October 16, 2026 (Developer API) / October 20, 2026 (Agent Platform). The Developer API warning conflicts with the exact API page’s ongoing-access notice; no live availability claim is made.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Safety Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-text search of the October 2026 safety report for parameter counts and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite found no retrospective size disclosure. Parameter references concern evaluation difficulty, security of model weights, or stored knowledge; the distillation section concerns unauthorized extraction, not a disclosed Flash-Lite base or size.

sources.title: The Grounding Gap: How LLMs Anchor the Meaning of Abstract Concepts Differently from Humans
sources.publisher: Odysseas S. Chlapanis, Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis, and Christos H. Papadimitriou
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model parameter search surfaced plots including Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. Figures 2, 4 and 7 explicitly attribute closed-model sizes to estimates from Li (2026), arXiv:2604.24827, rather than Google specifications. Followed that reference in both original and revised versions; the plot is not accepted as a published Google parameter count.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity (v2)
sources.evidence: Read the original v1 and July 5 revised v2 after tracing the Grounding Gap citation. This is independent black-box factual-capacity estimation, not a Google size disclosure. The revised paper describes order-of-magnitude effective capacity with approximately threefold uncertainty in either direction, not precise counts. The full-model-results rows for gemini-2.5-flash-lite and its thinking mode leave known parameter count and estimated-parameter cells blank; neither version supplies a developer nominal total or an activated count for this model.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Updates to our family of thinking models
sources.evidence: Fresh June 17, 2025 release-post check: introduces Flash-Lite as a cost-effective upgrade from earlier Flash models with configurable thinking and compares capabilities. It does not identify an unchanged named base checkpoint or publish total/active parameter numbers. An upgrade or family relationship alone cannot supply a size.

name.note: Official exact-model title, preserving Flash-Lite punctuation.

developer.note: Google publishes and distributes the model; the development organization is Google DeepMind.

family.note: Retain the catalog’s normalized Flash-Lite subfamily key; official materials identify the Gemini 2.5 family and Flash-Lite variant.

release_date.note: Earliest public preview availability is June 17. The stable API ID launched July 22, but the GA announcement explicitly identifies the same underlying model. September Preview (09-2025) is a separate later variant.

open_weights.note: Google distributes this model through proprietary hosted APIs, with no public checkpoint or open-weight license in the reviewed release and model documentation.

license.note: Descriptive service/model licensing classification; Gemini API terms govern access. Documentation footer CC BY and sample-code Apache licenses do not license model weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-name count and lineage searches, complete original card, linked Gemini 2.5 report, release/API pages and later first-party comparisons found no developer-published nominal total or named base with a known size. Google explicitly equates the June preview and July stable model, but gives neither a size. Teacher-output distillation does not establish parameter equality with a teacher. The new Grounding Gap plot lead traces to independent factual-capacity estimates, not a Google specification; no estimate is substituted.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 check confirms qualitative sparse MoE activation only. The full original card and later Flash-Lite comparison tables give no numerical activated-parameter count, expert count or routing width from which one could establish it. The independent factual-capacity research concerns effective total capacity and supplies no activated-count specification. No total, benchmark score, throughput or thinking budget is treated as an active size.

architecture.note: The exact Flash-Lite card explicitly describes sparse mixture-of-experts Transformers with native text, vision and audio input support. Detailed expert/layer counts are not supplied.

context_window.note: Exact API documentation labels this the input-token limit. The 65,536 output-token limit is a separate quantity.

modalities.note: Exact stable model table explicitly lists each input and text output; audio/image generation and Live API are not supported.

reasoning.note: Thinking is supported and optionally enabled; support does not imply it is always enabled.

tool_call.note: Exact stable-model capabilities table explicitly supports function calling.

description.value: Gemini 2.5 multimodal model with optional thinking and function calling.
description.note: Directly documented input scope and optional capabilities, without comparative performance or price claims.

patch.notes: First public preview: June 17, 2025. Stable API ID: July 22; Google explicitly says it uses the same underlying model. September Preview (09-2025) is separate. Sparse MoE Transformer; Google has not published total or active parameter counts. Availability documentation conflicts: the API page retains access for previous users while Firebase lists an October 16, 2026 shutdown warning.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: retain explicit nulls for total and active parameters after fresh exact-model searches, complete original-card and Gemini 2.5 technical-report checks, release/API documentation, and later 3.1/3.5 Flash-Lite, Gemini 4 Argon and safety comparisons. Clarify that the technical report does discuss the June Flash-Lite preview, but provides no numerical size. The June preview and July stable identity is documented; no known-size base or teacher-size equivalence is established. Trace a newly found parameter-plot lead through the Grounding Gap paper to Li’s independent black-box capacity study, whose v2 explicitly limits the method to uncertain effective-capacity estimates and gives no known count for Flash-Lite. Preserve all other audited fields, including earliest public release, capabilities and the recorded availability-documentation conflict.
